title: Elliptic curves, Part II: Legendre models, descent and character interfaces
summary: This Part II supplies equation-level Legendre models and all six labelled root-ordering parameters for rational curves with full two-torsion. It reads the existing descent map through the split cubic, derives good-prime unit and primitive-character conductor interfaces, and exports explicit two-primary torsion, corrected halving witnesses and trace identities over finite prime fields. Generic elliptic, character, conductor and twist-factor theories retain their existing owners.
readme:
# Elliptic curves, Part II: Legendre models, descent and character interfaces

This Part II extends the existing Tau Ceti EllipticCurves roadmap. It starts after the Weierstrass equations, point group, torsion, reduction, native quadratic twists and x−θ descent map supplied by its Layers 2–6. Its new library consists of concrete Legendre equations, labelled root-ordering parameters, rational good-prime unit and character-support interfaces, split-cubic readings of the existing descent, and explicit finite-field torsion and trace results.

The two domains are separated. Coefficient models are defined over commutative rings; torsion and descent use fields of characteristic not two and nonsingular parameters. Rational parameters use additive p-adic valuations and minimal local reduction. Finite-field exports use prime fields with explicit residue congruences. The six parameter labels are retained even when their values coincide at −1,2,1/2. Scaled models are twists, not automatically isomorphic to the unscaled model over the ground field.

The primitive character of a rational squareclass belongs to ClassicalArithmeticCompletion CA.1. Generic twist Euler factors belong to RankZeroOneBSD BSD.0. Actual elliptic-conductor support is imported from ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations R01.3; it is not identified with an algorithmic Ogg exponent without that comparison. The moduli-level six Möbius transformations belong to ModularCurves 9E; this roadmap does not reconstruct that moduli theory. The progression application imports the outputs without imposing its large-exponent hypotheses on these generic statements.

The target-level plan has 37 declaration-sized nodes. All six layers are planned, not closed. Exact supplier requests and explicit prototype gaps are retained, and every implementation status is unchecked. The detailed reader contains the definitions, proof outlines, APIs, tests and source locators.

stages.title: Legendre equations and root orderings
stages.description:
The Legendre equation. For any commutative ring R and λ∈R, legendre λ is the existing WeierstrassCurve with coefficients a₁=a₃=a₆=0, a₂=−(1+λ), a₄=λ. Its equation is y²=x(x−1)(x−λ). This defines a model even at λ=0,1; no ellipticity is claimed there.

The scaled Legendre equation. For a commutative ring R and d,λ∈R, scaledLegendre d λ has coefficients (0,−d(1+λ),0,d²λ,0), hence equation y²=x(x−d)(x−dλ). For fields with 2≠0 it is the native quadraticTwistOf (legendre λ) with parameters (0,−d/4): its twisting discriminant is d, not 4d.

Six labelled Legendre parameters. For a field K, legendreParameters λ is the Fin 6-indexed tuple (λ,1/λ,1−λ,1/(1−λ),λ/(λ−1),(λ−1)/λ). Labelled entries are retained, including repetitions. Mathematical parameter assertions require λ≠0,1; the tuple is a total rational-expression construction but its degenerate values are not valid parameters.

Legendre discriminant and ellipticity. For every commutative ring, Δ(Lλ)=16λ²(1−λ)² and c₄(Lλ)=16(λ²−λ+1). Over a field with 2≠0, Lλ is elliptic iff λ≠0 and λ≠1; for these parameters its native j-invariant equals 256(λ²−λ+1)³/(λ²(1−λ)²). The identities form one simultaneous coefficient calculation.

Scaled Legendre discriminant. Δ(Ld,λ)=16d⁶λ²(1−λ)² and c₄(Ld,λ)=16d²(λ²−λ+1). For a field with 2≠0 and d≠0, Ld,λ is elliptic iff λ≠0,1; on elliptic models j(Ld,λ)=j(Lλ).

Root-ordering cross-ratios. Let e₀,e₁,e₂ be pairwise distinct in a field, and λ=(e₂−e₀)/(e₁−e₀). The cross-ratios obtained from root orders (012),(021),(102),(120),(210),(201) equal, respectively, the six entries of legendreParameters λ. Each lies outside {0,1}. Repetitions in values do not collapse the six root orderings.

Legendre normalization of a split cubic. Let W over a field K with 2≠0 be in native IsCharNeTwoNF normal form, with cubic f=(X−e₀)(X−e₁)(X−e₂) and pairwise distinct roots. Set d=e₁−e₀, λ=(e₂−e₀)/d. Translation x_old=x_new+e₀,y_old=y_new gives a native VariableChange C with C•W=scaledLegendre d λ. Hence W is a quadratic twist of Lλ in the precise native coefficient sense, d≠0 and λ≠0,1. Reordering roots yields exactly the six parameters, with the corresponding twist scalar recomputed.

Normalization from full rational two-torsion. If E/ℚ is an elliptic Weierstrass curve whose native rational point group has exactly four points killed by 2, there exist a native rational VariableChange C, d∈ℚ× and λ∈ℚ\{0,1} such that C•E=scaledLegendre d λ. All associated parameters are precisely the labelled six root-ordering parameters, allowing coincidences.

The three labelled two-torsion points. For a field K with 2≠0,d≠0,λ≠0,1, scaledLegendreTwoTorsion d λ is the Fin 3-indexed tuple of native points (0,0),(d,0),(dλ,0) of Ld,λ, each supplied with its native nonsingularity proof. Their y-coordinate is zero; the point at infinity is not an entry.

The native scalar-twist identity. Over a field with 2≠0, scaledLegendre d λ=(legendre λ).quadraticTwistOf 0 (−d/4). The native twisting discriminant 0²−4(−d/4) is exactly d, so the twist is elliptic iff d≠0 and Lλ is elliptic.

Exhaustion of Legendre two-torsion. On Ld,λ over a field with 2≠0,d≠0,λ≠0,1, a native point P is killed by doubling iff P=O or P is one of (0,0),(d,0),(dλ,0). These four points are distinct; hence the doubling kernel has cardinality 4.

stages.title: Good reduction and character conductors
stages.description:
Nonintegral Legendre parameters force nonintegral j. Let p be an odd rational prime and λ∈ℚ\{0,1}. Write a=v_p(λ), b=v_p(1−λ). If a<0 then b=a and v_p(j(Lλ))=2a<0. If a>0 then b=0 and v_p(j(Lλ))=−2a<0. If b>0 then a=0 and v_p(j(Lλ))=−2b<0. Consequently v_p(j(Lλ))≥0 implies a=b=0.

Parameters at good odd primes. Let F/ℚ be elliptic with full rational two-torsion, semistable away from 2, and let λ be any associated Legendre parameter. If an odd prime p is of good reduction for the curve F, then v_p(λ)=v_p(1−λ)=0. The reduction hypothesis is applied to a minimal equation of F over ℚ_p, not to the arbitrary displayed scaled Legendre model.

Nonsingular reduction of the unit Legendre model. For λ∈ℚ\{0,1} and an odd prime p with v_p(λ)=v_p(1−λ)=0, the coefficient model Lλ is integral over ℤ_p with unit discriminant. Its reduction is an elliptic Legendre model over 𝔽_p with parameter λ̄≠0,1; the curve has good reduction at p. This statement is about Lλ itself, not an arbitrary d-twist.

Odd support of the attached primitive character. Let F,λ be as in good-prime-units, let ω∈{1,−1,2,−2}, and let χ be the CA.1 primitive character of the nonzero rational squareclass ωλ, of conductor N. Every odd prime dividing N is a bad prime of F. Equivalently the odd prime support of N is contained in the bad odd prime set of F.

Odd character conductor divides the elliptic conductor. Under the preceding hypotheses, if M is the actual elliptic conductor of F and N is the primitive conductor of the CA.1 character of ωλ, then ordCompl[2](N) divides M. In particular at semistable odd primes it divides the squarefree odd part of M. The theorem permits N=1 and does not assert nontriviality of the odd conductor.

stages.title: Split-cubic readings of the native descent map
stages.description:
The Legendre split-cubic CRT. For Ld,λ under the nonsingularity hypotheses, scaledLegendreCrt d λ is the canonical root-evaluation ring equivalence A=K[X]/(X(X−d)(X−dλ)) ≃ K×K×K, in root order (0,d,dλ). It is an adapter for the native Affine.A étale algebra, not a replacement algebra.

Root readings of native squareclasses. scaledLegendreSquareclassEquiv d λ is the induced multiplicative equivalence from native M=Aˣ/(Aˣ)² to (Kˣ/(Kˣ)²)³, obtained from scaledLegendreCrt. It transports μ values; it defines neither a new generic descent homomorphism nor a new kernel theorem.

Native descent away from the roots. For an affine native point (x,y) on Ld,λ with x∉{0,d,dλ}, the split reading of μ(P) is ([x],[x−d],[x−dλ]), with all three representatives nonzero. The image of O is (1,1,1).

Native descent at the three two-torsion points. The split readings at T₀,T_d,T_dλ on Ld,λ are respectively ([d²λ],[−d],[−dλ]), ([d],[d²(1−λ)],[d(1−λ)]), and ([dλ],[d(λ−1)],[d²λ(λ−1)]). All representatives are nonzero. The entry at a root is the derivative product of the other two differences, not zero.

Product of the split descent coordinates. For every native point P on Ld,λ, the product of the three split readings of μ(P) is 1. This is the native normM condition read through the split algebra; it holds at O and at the two-torsion roots as well.

The Legendre halving criterion. For a native affine point P=(x,y) on Ld,λ over K with 2≠0,d≠0,λ≠0,1, there exists Q∈Ld,λ(K) with 2Q=P iff x,x−d,x−dλ are all squares in K. Here IsSquare includes 0, but zero is not passed to a unit squareclass. The criterion also covers the three two-torsion points.

Evaluation through the split-cubic CRT. The class of h(X) maps to (h(0),h(d),h(dλ)).

Unit-class root readings. For a native A unit u, its image is the triple of squareclasses of the three CRT unit evaluations.

stages.title: Two-primary torsion over prime fields
stages.description:
Two-by-four torsion over prime fields. Let p be prime, p≡3 mod4, and η∈𝔽_p\{0,1,−1}. The native point group of L_{η²}:y²=x(x−1)(x−η²) contains a subgroup additively isomorphic to ZMod 2 × ZMod 4. In particular 8 divides the native pointCount.

A half of the zero root on the minus-one model. Over a field K with 2≠0 and i²=−1, minusOneOrderFour i is the native point (i,1−i) on L_{−1}. Its double is (0,0), hence its order is exactly 4. Over 𝔽_p with p≡5 mod8 such i exists by the supplementary law at −1; this is the source application.

No order-eight point on the minus-one model. For p≡5 mod8 prime, L_{−1}(𝔽_p) has no point of exact order 8. Only (0,0) among the three nonzero two-torsion points is divisible by 2; each of its four halves has nonsquare first descent coordinate.

Exact two-adic order of the minus-one point count. For p prime with p≡5 mod8, v₂(pointCount(L_{−1}/𝔽_p))=3, equivalently 8 divides this positive integer and 16 does not divide it. The count is the full projective elliptic count, including O.

Doubling the minus-one half. 2•minusOneOrderFour i is the native point (0,0) on L_{−1}.

Order of the minus-one half. addOrderOf(minusOneOrderFour i)=4.

First descent class of the minus-one half. The first split coordinate of native μ at this point is the squareclass [i].

stages.title: Explicit order-four points in the twist by two
stages.description:
The corrected order-four witness. Over a field K with 2≠0, let t,v be nonzero, i²=−1 and 2t²+2v²=1, and put λ=2t². twistHalvingPoint t v i is the native point P=(2λ+4itv,8itv(t+iv)) on L_{2,λ}:y²=x(x−2)(x−2λ). The conditions imply λ≠0,1 and y(P)≠0. This algebraic construction is valid without any progression hypothesis; the source applies it at p≡5 mod8.

Doubling the corrected witness. Under the corrected-witness hypotheses, native doubling of P is exactly (2λ,0). With r=2t,s=2iv the tangent slope is r+s and the doubled coordinates are (r²,0).

Exact order four of the corrected witness. Under the corrected-witness hypotheses, addOrderOf P=4. In particular it is neither O nor two-torsion, although its double is a two-torsion point.

The witness’s third native descent coordinate. Under the corrected-witness hypotheses, the third split reading of native μ(P) is the nonzero squareclass [4itv]. Indeed x(P)−2λ=4itv; y(P)≠0 implies x(P) avoids all three roots.

stages.title: Trace and downstream interfaces
stages.description:
Trace zero for a symmetric split cubic. For p prime with p≡3 mod4 and u∈𝔽_p×, the native Weierstrass curve with equation y²=x(x−u)(x+u) has pointCount p+1 and frobeniusTrace 0. It is scaledLegendre u (−1), hence is elliptic. No CM distribution or Hasse-bound input is required.

Legendre specialization of the twist-factor interface. For p odd prime and d∈𝔽_p×,λ∉{0,1}, specialize the BSD.0 good-prime quadratic-twist comparison along the native identity Ld,λ=(Lλ).quadraticTwistOf 0 (−d/4): frobeniusTrace(Ld,λ)=quadraticChar(d)·frobeniusTrace(Lλ). The good Euler polynomial is 1−quadraticChar(d)a_p(Lλ)T+pT². In particular at p≡5 mod8 the d=2 trace is −a_p(Lλ). This node exports only the equation-specific identification; the generic Euler-factor theorem and rational bad-prime factors stay in BSD.0.
